oewn-00798638-v.learner: to refuse or turn away something or someone with contempt.
examples: She rejected his apology with a cold laugh and turned her back on him.

connotation.why: refusal made with contempt for what is refused

oewn-00808840-v.learner: to judge that something is wrong or not suitable.
examples: Her parents rejected the rude way he spoke to the servants.

oewn-02508565-v.learner: to not let someone come in or become a member.
examples: The club rejected him because he was too young to join.

oewn-02760892-v.learner: (of a body) to fight against, with its defences against disease, a tissue or organ put into it from outside.
examples: His body rejected the new kidney.

oewn-05852632-n.learner: a particular kind of thing, as judged by how it looks.
examples: She bought the same style of hat in blue.

oewn-05758160-n.learner: what most people like at a certain time.
examples: Wide trousers were the style that summer.

oewn-06802072-n.learner: the rules an editor gives for spelling, punctuation, capital letters and how the text looks on the page.
examples: The newspaper's style is to spell out numbers below ten.

oewn-04353589-n.learner: a pointed tool used for writing, drawing or cutting lines into a surface.
examples: The scribe pressed the style into the soft wax.

oewn-11697710-n.learner: in a flower, the narrow, long part of the pistil that lies between the ovary and the stigma.
examples: Pollen grows down through the style to reach the ovary.

oewn-01903854-n.learner: a thin part, shaped like a bristle or a tube, that sticks out from a body.
examples: The insect has a short style at the tip of its body.

oewn-08002070-n.learner: two people who spend time with each other or are linked together.
examples: The couple met every Sunday to walk by the river.

oewn-09280469-n.learner: something held together by two equal forces that push in opposite directions along parallel lines.
examples: The two hands turning the wheel act on it as a couple.

oewn-00654017-v.learner: to identify what something is, in the way a scientist who studies plants or animals does.
examples: Using the key at the back of the book, he distinguished the plant as a wild orchid.

oewn-02035003-v.learner: to make a division or a split.
examples: Just past the bridge, the road divides.

oewn-01560556-v.learner: to move apart, or to break apart.
examples: The crowd divided to let the doctor through.

oewn-00643760-v.learner: to do a division sum, working out how many times one number goes into another.
examples: If you divide twelve by three, you get four.

oewn-13502051-n.learner: the burning of things that catch fire easily, which gives off heat and light and often smoke.
examples: Most wild animals are afraid of fire.

oewn-14710347-n.learner: burning fuel that is used to cook food on.
examples: She set the pot of soup on the fire.

oewn-00989024-n.learner: the act of shooting guns or big guns at an enemy.
examples: The soldiers came under heavy fire from the hill.
The minister faced fire from his own party over the new tax.

oewn-07435035-n.learner: a very hard experience that tests a person.
examples: He had come through the fire of war a changed man.

oewn-14867017-n.learner: one of the four elements that people, following Empedocles, once thought made up the universe, linked with the body fluid called bile.
examples: The old thinkers held that everything was made of earth, air, water and fire.

oewn-06785951-n.learner: a legal agreement that says what must be paid or done, and what the penalty is if it is not.
examples: The firm signed an obligation to deliver the goods by May, with a fine for each day of delay.

oewn-13419414-n.learner: a written promise to pay back money that is owed.
examples: The bank bought the town's obligations, to be repaid within ten years.

oewn-00708009-v.learner: to put something forward so that others can think about it, examine it, criticise it, and so on.
examples: The scientist proposed a new theory of how the moon was formed.

oewn-02406665-v.learner: to put someone forward, or to name them as a choice for an office, an honour or a position.
examples: She proposed her friend for the post of club secretary.

examples: He's out tonight with the boys from work.

connotation.why: calls a grown man a boy, with familiarity

oewn-84496658-n.learner: an insulting word for a Black man, used as a racial slur.

connotation.why: racial slur that demeans its target

oewn-05821331-n.learner: anything that you love warmly or are deeply devoted to.
examples: Music was her great passion.

examples: Her passion made her quick to love and quick to anger.

oewn-14062661-n.learner: something that you want very much.
examples: Owning a horse had become her passion, and she saved every penny for one.

oewn-09204454-n.learner: a reason for believing or doing something that makes no sense but that you cannot resist.
examples: Gambling had become a passion he could not master, though he knew it would ruin him.
